newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo workers discontent to escalate - trade union.
newsitem.headline: Yugo workers discontent to escalate - trade union.

text.p: Yugoslavs are seen becoming increasingly discontented with their living standards and are likely to take to the streets unless the state urgently addresses their demands, a trade union leader said on Thursday.

"If there is no dialogue between the state and the workers, protests will grow soon, workers will leave factory compounds and take to the streets," Confederation of Autonomous Trade Unions of Yugoslavia President (SSSJ) Dragan Radulovic said.

"I think the state bodies and employers are not reacting to these problems expediently and are still not aware that it is the eleventh hour to open a dialogue with workers, and the trade union as a social partner."

Strikes have escalated since th end of war in the former Yugoslavia and international sanctions against Serbia and Montenegro, which comprise the new Yugoslav federation, were formally lifted last October, the SSSJ said in a report.

Independent economists estimate some 836,000 people are on "compulsory leave" in the country, another 400,000 receive no salaries, while 200,000 receive less than the minimum wage of 200 dinars ($35) per month.
The average wage in April was 733 dinars, while a monthly basket of food products for a family of four cost 1,485 dinars.
Yugoslavia has around 1.3 million pensioners, 2.3 million employed and 650,000 people living below the poverty line. According to official statistics, there are 840,000 registered as unemployed.

Schoolteachers have gone on several long strikes this year, while doctors, nurses and social workers have been providing minimum services for the past five weeks in protest over late wages. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4305
